title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting. This page belongs to the 'variations sur l'équation des lacets' (the genus-1 / M_{1,1} part of the Longue Marche material). There is a finite quotient 𝔊 of SL(2,ℤ)^ (profinite). It carries the images ρ (order dividing 6) and σ (order dividing 4) of the standard elliptic generators of SL(2,ℤ) = ℤ/4 *_{ℤ/2} ℤ/6. Here σ² = ρ³ = '−1'.

G_{ρ,σ} is a group, built on earlier pages, that contains 𝔊. B_{ρ,σ} is a subgroup with B_{ρ,σ} ∩ 𝔊 = L_0. Z_σ is the centralizer in G_{ρ,σ} of L_σ = ⟨σ⟩.

Step (35). Using formulas (2),(4), the element τ_B := (τ,−1) lies in B_{ρ,σ}. Here τ is the image of the reflection τ_∞ = diag(−1,1) ∈ GL(2,ℤ), i.e. the extra generator obtained by passing to a quotient 𝔊' = {1,τ}·𝔊 of GL(2,ℤ)^. Clearly τ_B ∉ L_0 = B ∩ 𝔊.

Step (36). Hence there is an embedding 𝔊' ↪ G_{ρ,σ} with τ ↦ τ_B and g ↦ g on 𝔊. The action of τ on 𝔊 is then read as conjugation by τ_B.

Step (37)–(38). Since τ_B(σ) = σ^{-1}, the element τ_B normalizes L_σ and therefore normalizes its centralizer Z_σ. Grothendieck forms the abstract semidirect product N_σ = {1,τ_B} ⋉ Z_σ ('½ direct') with the canonical map i_σ : N_σ → G_{ρ,σ}.

Image of i_σ. It is the normalizer of L_σ. Any g normalizing L_σ, which is cyclic of order dividing 4, must send σ to a generator, i.e. to σ^{±1}.
- If g(σ) = σ, then g ∈ Z_σ.
- If g(σ) = σ^{-1} = τ_B(σ), then τ_B^{-1}g ∈ Z_σ, i.e. g ∈ τ_B Z_σ.

Injectivity (finished on the next page). i_σ is injective iff τ_B ∉ Z_σ, iff σ ≠ σ^{-1}, iff '−1' ≠ 1 in 𝔊.

What it serves. This is the standard description of the normalizer of an elliptic (torsion) subgroup in a finite quotient of the (extended) modular group. In geometric terms, these are the decomposition/inertia-type groups at the orbifold points j = 1728 (σ) and j = 0 (ρ), enlarged by the 'complex conjugation' reflection. The next page does the same for ρ using τ' = σ^{-1}τ (matrix [[0,1],[1,0]]). It then builds epimorphisms δ_ρ, δ_σ from N_ρ, N_σ onto a group 𝔊_{ρ,σ}, presumably feeding a local analysis of the 'equation des lacets' at the two elliptic points.
errors: Minor: 'le normalisateur de σ' should read 'normalisateur de L_σ = ⟨σ⟩'. The argument given is for the normalizer of the subgroup; the normalizer of the element σ itself is just Z_σ.
Implicit assumption: τ_B² = 1 is needed for {1,τ_B}⋉Z_σ to be a semidirect product with ℤ/2. It presumably follows from τ² = 1 and (−1)² = 1, but it is not stated.
First line lacks 'a' ('on [a]'). This is a slip, not a mathematical error. Otherwise the reasoning is correct: units of ℤ/4 (and ℤ/6, next page) are ±1, so the only generators are σ^{±1}.

ideas.what: Extending a finite quotient of SL(2,ℤ)^ to a quotient 𝔊' of GL(2,ℤ)^ by adjoining the reflection τ = diag(−1,1), realized inside G_{ρ,σ} as τ_B = (τ,−1)
ideas.modern_name: Extended modular group / real structure (complex conjugation) acting on finite-index subgroups; GL₂ vs SL₂ quotients
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical (extended modular group); in the Galois-Teichmüller context, the complex-conjugation element of GT and of the Teichmüller tower (Drinfeld, Ihara, Schneps)
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme mentions the role of complex conjugation; exact construction unsure

ideas.what: Normalizer of the cyclic subgroup generated by an elliptic element equals centralizer extended by an inverting involution; injectivity iff the element is not of order ≤2
ideas.modern_name: N(⟨x⟩) = ⟨t⟩⋉C(⟨x⟩) when Aut-image is {±1}; local/decomposition groups at elliptic points of modular curves

deep.surprise_reason: A routine group-theoretic step (normalizers of elliptic subgroups in finite quotients of the extended modular group) within a longer construction. It is correct and clean, but contains nothing a specialist would find new.
transcription_corrections: Line 1: 'd'après (2), (4) on [a]' — the (4) is an added reference beside (2), not a replacement.

Margin: the matrix is τ_∞ (written 't_∞') = [[−1,0],[0,1]]. The margin note says 'NB 𝔊' est un quotient de GL(2,ℤ)^, et τ correspond à l'image de l'élément t_∞ de GL(2,ℤ)', consistent with page 540's τ'_∞ = −σ_∞τ_∞ = [[0,1],[1,0]].
